door_close.description: Close the garage door. Same caution as door_open: a closing door is the one that can trap something.

door_open.description: Open the garage door. Moves a heavy motorised door — gate this behind a deliberate action and check the reported state and obstruction sensor first.

door_set_position.description: Drive the door to a position, 0.0 closed to 1.0 open. Security+ 2.0 only.
door_set_position.notes: The position argument rides the query string (`/cover/Door/set?position=0.5`), which is how ESPHome's web_server takes it. The board answers 409 if the cover does not support position at all, which is the Security+ 1.0 case.

position.description: Target position on ESPHome's cover scale: 0.0 fully closed, 1.0 fully open — `min`/`max` bound the RAW wire value. NOT a percentage on the wire, so `scale: 100` states the decoded terms: a UI's 0-100% slider value divides by 100 to encode (raw = value / scale). The device clamps out-of-range values, so sending a raw 50 for "half open" drives the door fully open instead.

door_stop.description: Halt a door mid-travel. Security+ 2.0 only — Sec+ 1.0 openers have no stop.

lock_remotes.description: Engage the opener's remote lock-out, so paired remotes stop working.

restart_board.description: Reboot the ratgdo board. Does not move the door.

txt_match.description: `esphome: project: name:` from the ratgdo board configs. A node whose project_name does not start `ratgdo.` is some other ESPHome device and belongs to esphome-device.yaml.

mdns_txt_match.description: ESPHome publishes the firmware's `esphome: project: name:` as the project_name TXT record. Every published ratgdo board config sets it to `ratgdo.<board>` — v25iboard_secplus2, v32board_secplus2, v2board_esp8266_d1_mini_lite — so the prefix matches the family and nothing else on the platform.

device.name: ratgdo Garage-Door Controller (ESPHome)
device.notes:
ratgdo is a small ESP board wired to a Chamberlain/LiftMaster opener's wall-control terminals; it speaks the opener's Security+ 1.0/2.0 wire protocol (see chamberlain-garage-opener-secplus.yaml for that side) and exposes local, cloud-free control on the home network. This spec targets the mainstream ESPHome ratgdo firmware.
NOT EVERY ESPHome NODE IS A ratgdo. ratgdo is one product built on ESPHome, and _esphomelib._tcp is the service type of the PLATFORM: a bedroom temperature sensor, a bluetooth proxy and a garage-door controller all publish it. Identify a ratgdo by the `project_name` TXT record, which the board configs set to `ratgdo.<board>` (observed values `ratgdo.v25iboard_secplus2`, `ratgdo.v32board_secplus2`, `ratgdo.v2board_esp8266_d1_mini_lite`) — hence the `ratgdo.` prefix matcher in `identification.mdns_txt_match`. An ESPHome node that does NOT match it is esphome-device.yaml's, and rendering it as a garage door is the exact failure that matcher exists to prevent. Konnected's blaQ is ratgdo-compatible hardware: flashed with mainstream ratgdo firmware it matches like any other board, but Konnected's own build sets its own project_name, which has not been observed here — so this matcher does not claim it, and a blaQ on stock firmware falls to the generic ESPHome spec until somebody dumps its TXT records.
Two interchangeable local transports, both no-cloud, no-broker: 1. WEB SERVER (HTTP :80) — enabled by default in ratgdo's config. A plain
   REST API plus a Server-Sent-Events state stream, ideal for a phone app:
     POST /cover/Door/open | /close | /stop | /toggle
     POST /cover/Door/set?position=<0.0..1.0>  (Security+ 2.0 only)
     GET  /cover/Door                          -> JSON state
     POST /light/Light/turn_on | /turn_off | /toggle
     POST /lock/Lock%20remotes/lock | /unlock
     GET  /binary_sensor/{Obstruction,Motion,Motor,Button}
     POST /button/Restart/press
     GET  /events  (text/event-stream) -> "state" events with the same
          per-entity JSON, the push channel for door/obstruction/motion.
   JSON state shape per entity, e.g.
     {"id":"cover/Door","state":"OPEN","current_operation":"IDLE","position":1.0}
     {"id":"binary_sensor/Obstruction","value":true,"state":"ON"}
   Default has NO auth; if the user adds web_server auth (basic/digest) the
   app must send it. web_server "version" affects only the built-in UI, not
   these endpoints.
2. NATIVE API (TCP :6053, protobuf) — always present, what Home Assistant
   uses. Length-delimited protobuf: Hello -> Connect -> ListEntities (match
   the entity to its numeric key) -> SubscribeStates; commands reference the
   entity key. Framing byte 0x00 = plaintext, 0x01 = Noise-encrypted
   (Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256 with the 32-byte base64 PSK from
   `api: encryption: key:`). Efficient and streaming, but heavier to
   implement than the REST/SSE path; prefer the web server for a first cut.
   The legacy `api: password:` was removed in ESPHome 2026.1.0 (deprecated
   since 2022), so a current build is plaintext or Noise, never password.

ADDRESSING — WHICH NAME GOES IN THE URL. ESPHome changed this, and a client that hardcodes one form breaks on half the fleet:
  * ESPHome <= 2025.12: the URL segment is the entity's slugified
    object_id, and the JSON `id` field is `<domain>-<object_id>`
    (`/cover/door`, `{"id":"cover-door"}`).
  * ESPHome 2026.1.0 through 2026.6: URLs match the entity NAME first and
    fall back to object_id with a deprecation warning — both forms work.
    2026.1.3+ also publishes the new-form identifier in a `name_id` field
    alongside the legacy `id`.
  * ESPHome >= 2026.7: the object_id fallback is gone from URL matching.
    URLs are the entity NAME, percent-encoded (`/cover/Door`,
    `/lock/Lock%20remotes/lock`).
  * ESPHome >= 2026.8: the JSON identifier catches up — `id` itself carries
    `<domain>/<name>` and `name_id` is no longer sent. Note this is a
    SECOND, later boundary: on 2026.7 the URL is already name-only while
    `id` is still the legacy `<domain>-<object_id>`, so a client that
    derives the URL from `id` breaks on exactly that release.
The `path` of every command below is the NAME form, which is what current ratgdo firmware needs (its base config requires ESPHome >= 2026.4), and each carries the legacy object_id form as `path_fallback` so a board that predates the change stays drivable from this file: send `path`, and on a 404 send `path_fallback`. Entities carry the same pair as `state_topic` / `state_topic_fallback`. A client that would rather not probe reads the identifier out of /events instead: an `id` containing `/` is the new form, anything else is the legacy one. Either way, a wrong form is a 404 and never a silent no-op — which is what makes the fallback safe, and why it must be gated on the 404 rather than on a timeout.
ENTITY NAMES (object_id in brackets, for the legacy form): cover `Door` [door] (JSON `state` is OPEN or CLOSED only — travel shows up in `current_operation` as OPENING/CLOSING/IDLE; actions open/close/stop/ toggle/set); light `Light` [light]; lock `Lock remotes` [lock_remotes] (lock/unlock); read-only binary_sensors `Obstruction`, `Motion`, `Motor`, `Button`; sensors `Openings`, `Paired Devices` [paired_devices]; text_sensor `Firmware Version` [firmware_version]; buttons `Restart`, `Toggle door`, `Sync`, `Query status`, `Query openings`; numbers `Opening duration`, `Closing duration`, `Rolling code counter`, `Client ID`; switch `Learn` (pairing mode). The phone app's core four: the cover, the light, the remote lock-out, and the read-only sensors.
GENERATION CAVEAT: on Security+ 1.0 openers the door has no stop/position (the opener does not support it) — expose stop/position only for Sec+ 2.0.
SAFETY: this opens/closes a heavy motorised door. Treat door commands as advanced; gate them on the reported door state and surface obstruction.
Cloud dependency: none. The native API is a direct device<->app socket; the web server is served from the board. No broker, no account.

issued_to_client: The native-API Noise PSK, if the user chose an encrypted build, must be shared with the app
credentials.notes: The web server is unauthenticated by default (add web_server auth to change that). The native API is plaintext or Noise-encrypted — the legacy `api: password:` was removed in ESPHome 2026.1.0. Detect which from the mDNS TXT: `api_encryption` means a PSK is set and Noise is required, `api_encryption_supported` means the build can do Noise but has no key yet and still accepts plaintext.
stored_on_device: Optional native-API Noise PSK (api: encryption: key)

factory_reset.effect: Re-flashing or an ESPHome factory-reset clears Wi-Fi credentials and the ESPHome config; the opener pairing (rolling-code seed) is separate and cleared at the opener's learn button. The exact ratgdo reset procedure (button hold vs re-flash) is not established here.

methods.description: ESPHome captive-portal / improv provisioning to join Wi-Fi, then local HTTP/native-API control. (ratgdo images are flashed via the web installer at ratgdo.github.io or Konnected's installer.)

steps.action: Flash ratgdo ESPHome firmware and wire the board to the opener terminals; pair with the opener's learn button.
Join the board to Wi-Fi (ESPHome AP/improv, or flashed credentials).
Discover it via _esphomelib._tcp mDNS; read the project_name TXT to confirm it is a ratgdo (vs any other ESPHome device, which the same service type also finds).
steps.expect: TXT project_name starts `ratgdo.`; the web server answers GET /cover/Door (older firmware: /cover/door) with the door state.

setup.notes: Two-part setup. HARDWARE: wire the ratgdo board to the opener's wall-control terminals and pair it to the opener with the opener's learn button (see chamberlain-garage-opener-secplus.yaml). NETWORK: the board is an ESPHome device — on first boot it hosts a Wi-Fi provisioning AP (or is flashed with credentials); once on the LAN it advertises _esphomelib._tcp and answers the web server on :80 and the native API on :6053. Confidence medium: standard ESPHome flows, not yet run here. Discriminate plaintext vs Noise-encrypted native API by the presence of the mDNS `api_encryption` TXT key; the web server has no such gate.

rejoin.notes: Standard ESPHome Wi-Fi rejoin; identity keys on the board MAC (mDNS TXT `mac`), not IP, so a DHCP move does not lose it.

testing.notes: Written from the authoritative ESPHome ratgdo config and ESPHome docs; no hardware driven yet (board on order). The control surface is standard ESPHome, so the endpoints are well-established, but the ratgdo entity names and the default-on web_server should be confirmed on the first real board — along with which addressing form that board's firmware accepts (see ADDRESSING below). Discovery (_esphomelib._tcp) will be exercised by the app's existing mDNS meta-query sweep; the project_name TXT matcher that separates a ratgdo from every other ESPHome node is read from the published board configs, not yet from a live TXT dump.

entities.name: Garage Door
entities.notes: Entity name 'Door' (object_id 'door' on ESPHome <= 2025.12). JSON `state` is OPEN or CLOSED; travel is reported separately in `current_operation` (OPENING/CLOSING/IDLE). The state_mapping paths are the reply fields the JSON-shape example in device.notes shows; `position` (0.0..1.0) is absent on Security+ 1.0 covers, which do not support position.

entities.name: Garage Light
entities.notes: The light reply's `state` field is the string "ON" or "OFF" (the same state-string convention the binary_sensor example in device.notes shows), per the ESPHome Web Server API doc — reported, not yet read from hardware.

entities.name: Lock Remotes
entities.notes: ESPHome exposes this in the `lock` domain (entity name 'Lock remotes', lock/unlock); modelled here as a switch (on = remotes locked out) because this schema's entity vocabulary has no lock platform. On = the opener ignores its RF remotes. The lock reply's `state` field carries the lock-domain state string, LOCKED or UNLOCKED, per the ESPHome Web Server API doc — reported, not yet read from hardware.

entities.name: Obstruction
entities.notes: The reply's `value` field is JSON true/false (the shape example in device.notes: {"value":true,"state":"ON"}), so it needs no on_when/on_value — the value IS the on/off.

entities.name: Openings
entities.notes: Cumulative door-open counter (entity name 'Openings'); the reply's numeric `value` field carries the count.

http_endpoints.description: JSON state of the garage door cover: `state` OPEN or CLOSED (any position but fully closed reads OPEN), `current_operation` OPENING/CLOSING/IDLE, `value` a float 0.0..1.0. `position` is present only when the cover supports position — Security+ 2.0 — so its absence is the Sec+ 1.0 case, not an error. Legacy path /cover/door.
http_endpoints.name: Door State

http_endpoints.description: Open the garage door. Siblings: /cover/Door/close, /cover/Door/stop, /cover/Door/toggle. Advanced: moves a heavy motorised door. Legacy path /cover/door/open.
http_endpoints.name: Open Door

http_endpoints.description: Set door position: query param position=<0.0..1.0>, ESPHome's cover scale (0.0 closed, 1.0 open) — not a percentage. Security+ 2.0 only (Sec+ 1.0 openers have no position/stop), and the device answers 409 if the cover does not support position. Advanced.
http_endpoints.name: Set Door Position

http_endpoints.description: Turn the garage light on. Siblings: /light/Light/turn_off, /light/Light/toggle. Legacy path /light/light/turn_on.
http_endpoints.name: Light On

http_endpoints.description: Engage the opener's remote lock-out. Sibling: /lock/Lock%20remotes/unlock. The entity is named 'Lock remotes', so the space is percent-encoded; legacy path /lock/lock_remotes/lock.
http_endpoints.name: Lock Remotes

http_endpoints.description: Reboot the ratgdo board. Does not affect the door. Legacy path /button/restart/press.
http_endpoints.name: Restart Board

http_endpoints.description: text/event-stream; emits 'state' events carrying the same per-entity JSON as the REST GETs — the push channel for door/obstruction/motion changes without polling. Also 'ping' and 'log' events. Every entity's current state is sent on connect, which is also how a client learns which addressing form this firmware uses (an `id` containing '/' is the name form; 2026.1.3-2026.7 firmware carries the new form in `name_id` beside a legacy `id`, and on 2026.7 the URL is name-only while `id` is still legacy — read `name_id` first).
http_endpoints.name: State Event Stream (SSE)

covers: Open / close / stop / toggle the door
Door position/state, obstruction, motion, motor, wall-button status
local_access.summary: Fully local control (ESPHome web server REST/SSE on :80 and native protobuf API on :6053) with no cloud and no broker. This is the network-facing counterpart to the Security+ wired protocol.
